461: B is correct because AWS Global Accelerator uses anycast IP addresses at AWS edge locations to route user traffic over the AWS global backbone to the nearest healthy endpoint, providing the lowest possible latency for a globally used application. A Network Load Balancer supports both TCP and UDP listeners, so it can handle both traffic types behind the accelerator endpoint, whereas an Application Load Balancer does not support UDP. The Auto Scaling group registers its instances with the NLB so traffic is distributed to healthy servers. CloudFront is a caching service for HTTP and HTTPS content and cannot proxy raw TCP and UDP traffic.
462: B is correct because writing incoming orders to an Amazon SQS queue durably buffers them, so orders are captured reliably and as quickly as possible even when the database cannot keep up during traffic spikes. EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group behind an Application Load Balancer can then pull messages from the queue and process them into Aurora at a sustainable rate, with the group able to scale based on queue depth. This decoupling ensures no orders are lost during high traffic. SNS cannot subscribe a database endpoint directly, and threshold-based or scheduled scaling cannot guarantee immediate and reliable order writes.
463: C is correct because AWS Lambda is the most cost-effective option for this tiny workload, charging only for the milliseconds of execution with no idle infrastructure cost. The job processes about 2 MB of data per mattress, needs 1 GB of memory, and completes within 30 seconds, which fits easily within Lambda limits of 10 GB of memory and 15 minutes of runtime. AWS Glue and Amazon EMR provision or manage heavier ETL and big data frameworks that would cost far more than necessary for such a small, short task.
464: A is correct because converting the existing RDS instance to a Multi-AZ deployment is a simple modification of the DB instance, requires no application changes, and keeps the same connection endpoint. RDS automatically maintains a synchronous standby replica in another Availability Zone and fails over to it if the primary becomes unavailable, eliminating the single point of failure and minimizing downtime. Creating a new deployment from a snapshot takes more effort, and read replicas with Route 53 weighted records require application changes and rely on asynchronous replication rather than automatic failover.
465: C is correct because EBS Multi-Attach, which allows a single volume to be attached to and written by multiple Nitro-based EC2 instances at the same time within the same Availability Zone, is supported only by Provisioned IOPS SSD io2 volumes. The io2 volumes provide the high IOPS and durability needed for the application to write to the shared block volume across multiple instances for higher availability. General Purpose SSD gp3 and gp2 volumes and Throughput Optimized HDD st1 volumes do not support Multi-Attach.
466: A is correct because the application tier in a single Availability Zone is the remaining single point of failure, since the RDS database is already Multi-AZ. Deploying the stateless EC2 instances across multiple Availability Zones with an Auto Scaling group behind an Application Load Balancer makes the application highly available, with the ALB distributing traffic and the Auto Scaling group automatically replacing unhealthy instances. Route 53 latency routing and cross-Region snapshots do not remove the single-AZ application tier as a failure point, and Route 53 rules alone cannot balance or health-check the tier.
467: B is correct because Savings Plan discount sharing for accounts in an organization is enabled from the Billing preferences of the AWS Organizations management (payer) account, not from the member account that purchased the plan. Once discount sharing is turned on, the Compute Savings Plan rates apply to eligible usage across all accounts in the organization, so other accounts can consume the unused commitment. This lets the organization capture the full benefit of the plan without migrating workloads. Savings Plan commitments cannot be sold in the Reserved Instance Marketplace.
468: B is correct because the requirement is to present REST APIs to users, and an Amazon API Gateway REST API is the purpose-built service for this, whereas a WebSocket API is designed for stateful, real-time bidirectional communication. Hosting the containers in Amazon ECS within private subnets keeps the backend services isolated, and a VPC link provides API Gateway the private connectivity it needs to reach services in the private VPC subnets without exposing them to the internet. A security group alone cannot provide the public API Gateway service with a private network path into the VPC.
469: C is correct because S3 Intelligent-Tiering automatically moves objects between frequent, infrequent, and archive access tiers based on actual access patterns, which is exactly what is needed when the access pattern is unpredictable and cannot be controlled. Lifecycle transitions to S3 Standard-IA would require guessing which objects are infrequently accessed and could incur retrieval charges if guess wrong, whereas Intelligent-Tiering has no retrieval fees and requires no monitoring. S3 replication is for copies in other buckets or Regions, and S3 Inventory only reports on objects without performing transitions.
470: D is correct because an egress-only internet gateway is designed specifically for IPv6 and allows outbound connections from the EC2 instances to the internet while blocking inbound connections initiated from outside, satisfying the security policy. A regular internet gateway would permit bidirectional traffic including externally initiated connections. NAT gateways do not support IPv6, and a virtual private gateway is used for VPN or Direct Connect connectivity rather than internet egress.
471: C is correct because a gateway VPC endpoint for Amazon S3 adds routes to the VPC route tables so that S3 traffic travels over the AWS private network and never traverses the internet, meeting the isolation requirement. Gateway endpoints are offered at no additional charge, which minimizes costs for the 1 TB of daily data. An interface endpoint would also keep traffic private but incurs hourly and per-GB data processing charges that are unnecessary for S3.
472: A is correct because Amazon DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX) is a fully managed, purpose-built cache that delivers microsecond-level latency for DynamoDB reads. The only application change needed is to point existing calls at the DAX endpoint, satisfying the minimal-change requirement, while DAX handles caching and write-through automatically. Increasing read capacity units still leaves millisecond latency and higher cost, DynamoDB does not offer read replicas in that sense, and adding ElastiCache for Redis would require significantly more application rework.
473: A is correct because Amazon CloudFront caches the static content at edge locations close to users, so most requests are served from the cache instead of hitting the EC2 instances and ALB. This offloads load from the origin, reduces the need for additional EC2 capacity, and lowers data transfer and compute costs as traffic grows. AWS WAF cannot cache content, ElastiCache behind an ALB does not serve static files to users, and deploying a second ALB in another Region adds cost without caching.
474: C is correct because an AWS Transit Gateway acts as a regional network hub, so each VPC in a Region needs only a single attachment to communicate with all other VPCs in that Region, avoiding the management of many individual connections. Transit Gateway peering then connects the regional hubs across Regions, providing transitive any-to-any connectivity across all Regions with the least administrative effort. VPC peering is non-transitive and would require a nearly full mesh of connections, Direct Connect gateways connect on-premises networks to VPCs, and PrivateLink provides one-way private service access rather than general VPC-to-VPC communication.
475: C is correct because Amazon EFS is a highly durable shared file system for containerized workloads and provides a mount target in each Availability Zone of the Region, so ECS tasks can mount the same file system from any AZ. EFS integrates with AWS Backup, which can manage cross-Region replication to satisfy the 8-hour RPO requirement for recovering data to another Region. The FSx file systems serve specific protocols such as SMB, NFS via ONTAP, or OpenZFS and do not provide a mount target in every Availability Zone the way EFS does, making them a poorer fit for this regional container workload.
476: C is correct because the standard and most secure way to grant permissions to groups of users is to create an IAM policy that grants only least-privilege permissions and attach it to the IAM group, so every user added to a departmental group automatically inherits exactly the access they need. IAM roles cannot be attached to IAM groups, as roles are assumed for delegation scenarios such as federated users or services rather than granting standing permissions to group members. SCPs set the maximum available permissions in the organization but do not themselves grant access to users.
477: D is correct because s3:DeleteObject is an object-level action, so the policy must allow it on the objects within the bucket, which are addressed by the resource arn:aws:s3:::bucket-name/* with the slash and asterisk. The current policy grants DeleteObject only on the bucket ARN itself, which is why the group cannot delete objects. s3:ListBucket is a bucket-level action that is already correctly scoped to the bucket resource, and the fix preserves least-privilege access.
478: B is correct because S3 Object Lock with a retention period set in accordance with the designated date prevents any modification or deletion of object versions, even by administrators, until the retention period expires, which is the most secure way to enforce immutability. S3 Versioning is required for Object Lock, static website hosting serves the files publicly, and a bucket policy granting read-only access makes the hundreds of files publicly readable. IAM read-only permissions apply only to AWS principals rather than the general public, and a Lambda function that restores modified objects is far less secure and reliable than Object Lock.
479: B is correct because AWS CloudFormation lets the company define the entire validated prototype infrastructure, the Auto Scaling group, Application Load Balancer, and RDS database, as a reusable template and then deploy it automatically and consistently into development and production environments across two Availability Zones. This infrastructure as code approach eliminates manual provisioning errors and enables immediate repeatable deployments. AWS Systems Manager and AWS Config are not designed to provision new environments from an existing configuration, and Elastic Beanstalk cannot reference a hand-built prototype as an automated deployment template.
480: B is correct because a VPC endpoint enables connectivity between the EC2 instances and Amazon S3 over the AWS private network, so encrypted application traffic between the services never traverses the public internet, meeting the compliance requirement. A gateway VPC endpoint for S3 works through route table entries, keeping the data path entirely on the AWS backbone. AWS KMS manages encryption keys but does not control the network path, a private subnet alone still sends S3 traffic over the internet without an endpoint, and a virtual private gateway is for VPN or Direct Connect connectivity to on-premises networks.
